answer: A newly spawned identity starts hollow, with no attestations, so it cannot forge peer endorsements without burning real stake that slashes on any proven duplicate. Participants must stake a bond locked to a verifiable hardware root and post a slowly maturing reputation history before voting on epoch challenges. Because each identity's bond matures toward a distant horizon, cheap mass registration fails: an attacker pays the full bond per clone and loses it all when correlation analysis exposes shared infrastructure. In practice, Agent0153 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
